title: 2019 HMMT November Guts Problem 13
statement: In \(\triangle A B C\), the incircle centered at \(I\) touches sides \(A B\) and \(B C\) at \(X\) and \(Y\), respectively. Additionally, the area of quadrilateral \(B X I Y\) is \(\frac{2}{5}\) of the area of \(A B C\). Let \(p\) be the smallest possible perimeter of a \(\triangle A B C\) that meets these conditions and has integer side lengths. Find the smallest possible area of such a triangle with perimeter \(p\).

solutions.text:
Answer: \(2 \sqrt{5}\)
Note that \(\angle B X I=\angle B Y I=90\), which means that \(A B\) and \(B C\) are tangent to the incircle of \(A B C\) at \(X\) and \(Y\) respectively. So \(B X=B Y=\frac{A B+B C-A C}{2}\), which means that \(\frac{2}{5}=\frac{[B X I Y]}{[A B C]}=\frac{A B+B C-A C}{A B+B C+A C}\). The smallest perimeter is achieved when \(A B=A C=3\) and \(B C=4\). The area of this triangle \(A B C\) is \(2 \sqrt{5}\).
